- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early days of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Forecast accuracy improves as horizon extends beyond 15 days, suggesting model struggles with short-term volatility.
- Model underreacts to strong downward trends in recent history — fails to anticipate sharp drops.
- When true outcome is below 70, model often overcorrects upward, suggesting it misinterprets low prices as temporary.
- Model shows lag in adjusting to recent price reversals — takes 2–3 days to reflect new trend direction.
- Forecast tends to be smoother than actual price movements — underestimates volatility spikes and overestimates consolidation periods.
